label: 邵氏武侠 · Shaw Brothers studio wuxia (1967–1983)
source: Shaw Brothers Studio retrospectives; Chor Yuen / Chang Cheh era surveys. The house look is soundstage-built: elaborate interior sets, gel-lit colour, a permanent artificial dusk.

look.image: 1970s Shaw Brothers studio wuxia still, shot entirely on a soundstage: painted backdrop horizon, permanent amber magic-hour glow, coloured gel lighting pooling in the corners of the frame, low-lying dry-ice mist across the floor, lacquered timber and silk banners, saturated primary costume colours against deep shadow, proscenium staging with the action centred and parallel to the camera, anamorphic-era Shawscope framing, rich Eastmancolor film stock with visible grain
look.video: studio-bound wuxia staging: the camera holds a clean wide proscenium and lets the choreography cross it; wire-assisted leaps land inside the frame; mist drifts, silk and banners move in the air
look.negatives: handheld shake, documentary realism, modern clothing, contemporary architecture, desaturated grey grading, natural overcast daylight, drone footage, lens flare from LED sources, plastic textures

camera.clause: one dominant move only, executed smoothly on a dolly or crane — never handheld

pacing.note: Shaw shots breathe: the set is the spectacle, so the frame is held long enough to read it.

notes: Warm amber highlights over cool shadows is the signature: an artificial sunset that never sets. Saturation is pushed hard — Shaw colour was a selling point against black-and-white wuxia.
